summary.en: The cultural and intellectual hub of Laramie, this area is defined by grand sandstone architecture, sprawling lawns, and the daily energy of student life.
Explore the compact downtown grid where the spirit of the Old West lives on in 19th-century facades and the stories of historic figures like Bill Nye.
Discover the quiet, contemplative side of Laramie in its community parks and poignant memorials, offering a glimpse into local life and national history.

description.en: A sprawling, park-like campus with a mix of classic sandstone buildings and modern structures, perfect for an aimless, atmospheric walk.
The heart of the original campus, this large, open lawn is a central green space surrounded by major academic buildings.
The student union building on the University of Wyoming campus, a hub of activity and the location of a significant memorial.
A self-guided exploration of historic downtown, imagining the town through the eyes of 19th-century humorist Edgar Wilson 'Bill' Nye who lived and worked here.
A key street in the historic downtown grid, perfect for discovering local eateries and observing 19th-century architecture.
One of downtown Laramie's main thoroughfares, offering opportunities to find local restaurants and soak in the historic atmosphere.
A powerful, understated memorial to the university student whose 1998 murder was a turning point for LGBTQ+ rights in America.
One of the city's oldest parks, this large, tree-filled expanse offers an authentic glimpse into local life and the town's unhurried pace.

prompt.en: Find the oldest and newest buildings you can see from one spot. Take a photo that captures both, showing the contrast in architectural styles.
Photograph a detail that could only exist on a university campus—a flyer for a club, a creatively decorated dorm window, or a well-used bike rack.
Find a piece of public art or sculpture and take a photo of it from an unusual angle—from ground level, through foliage, or capturing its reflection.
Take a selfie in front of the most impressive academic building you can find, striking a thoughtful, scholarly pose.
Many campuses have small, hidden gardens or quiet quads. Find one and capture a photo that conveys its peaceful atmosphere.
Get up close to one of the classic sandstone buildings and take a detailed photo of its texture and color.
Take a photo looking down a long, tree-lined path or walkway, emphasizing the lines and perspective.
Find the university's official colors (brown and gold) represented somewhere on campus and make them the subject of your photo.
Find a bench or patch of grass that looks like the absolute perfect place to study or read a book. Photograph it.
Capture an image that represents knowledge or learning—a library window, a lecture hall sign, or a statue of a historic figure.
Take a photo that captures the movement and energy of people walking between classes.
Photograph a scene where the natural, park-like landscape of the campus interacts with the man-made academic buildings.
Find a building facade that looks like it's straight out of the 1880s. Photograph it in black and white to enhance its historic feel.
Find a small architectural detail that evokes the Old West—faded paint on brick, an old-fashioned sign font, or ornate ironwork. Make it the focus of your photo.
Look for faint, painted advertisements on the sides of old brick buildings. Capture the best 'ghost sign' you can find.
Search for a cornerstone or historical marker with a date on it. Take a photo of the oldest date you can find in the neighborhood.
Take a selfie that blends the historic, Old West background with a modern element, like you listening to headphones or checking your phone.
Stand in a safe spot and take a photo looking down one of the long, straight streets of the downtown grid, emphasizing the sense of perspective.
The report mentions seeking out non-chain spots. Photograph the storefront of the most interesting-looking independent shop or eatery you see.
Capture a photo that shows a historic building next to a modern car or sign, highlighting the passage of time.
Look up! The most interesting architectural details are often on the second or third floors of old buildings. Photograph a cool window, cornice, or brick pattern above street level.
Find a modern window or puddle that reflects an old, historic building. Capture the reflection.
Use the late afternoon sun to capture dramatic shadows cast by the historic downtown buildings.
Channeling the spirit of humorist Bill Nye, find something in the streetscape that strikes you as quirky or funny and capture it in a photo.
Find a simple, empty park bench and take a photo of it. Try to capture a sense of peace and quiet dignity.
Find an open space in a park and take a photo that is at least two-thirds sky. Capture the vastness of the high-plains sky.
Without being intrusive, capture an image that shows how locals use these green spaces—a dog being walked, a game of catch, or someone reading on the grass.
Find the most ancient-looking tree in the area. Take a photo that emphasizes its gnarled bark, thick trunk, and character.
Find a peaceful spot and take a selfie looking thoughtful or reflective, with the natural or memorial background setting the mood.
Take a close-up photo of a natural texture: tree bark, a fallen leaf, blades of grass, or the surface of a stone.
Photograph the way sunlight filters through tree leaves, creating patterns of light and shadow on the ground.
Capture an image of a simple park feature—a water fountain, a swing set, a picnic table—that represents the idea of a shared community space.
Find any plaque or inscription on a bench, statue, or monument. Take a photo focusing on a few powerful words.
Take a photo of a scene that feels completely ordinary and authentic to Laramie, something a tourist might normally overlook.
Find a plant, tree, or flower that best represents the current season in Laramie and make it the star of your photograph.
Photograph a walking path as it curves and disappears into the distance, inviting a peaceful stroll.
